# Overview

In Lecture 05 and Worksheet 05 you learned **Quarto** — how one `.qmd` file holds your writing *and* your code, computes every number and figure, and renders to a professional Word document. No more copying results by hand.

This homework asks you to prove you can do it on your own analysis. You will take a **complete analysis you have already run** and rewrite it as a Quarto report that renders to Word.

> **Choose ONE analysis to write up:**
>
> - your **Cisco t-test** from Homework 03, **or**
> - the **paper calibration regression** from Worksheet 05 (Regression).

> **Submit to Canvas:** (1) your `.qmd` source file **and** (2) the rendered `.docx` Word document.

::: callout-tip
**Start from a template.** Open `leaf_report_template.qmd` from the Quarto worksheet (or `regression_analysis_report.qmd`) and adapt it — you do not have to start from a blank file.
:::

::: callout-warning
**✋ Parts 8 and 9 (below) must be answered by hand.** Write them on paper, take a clear photo, and embed the photo directly in your rendered report with a normal Markdown image link — `![](figures/q8_handwriting.jpg)` — saved into your project's `figures/` folder like any other image. A typed answer to Part 8 or 9 receives **at most half credit even if it is completely correct** — I am not grading whether the answer is right, I am grading whether *you* produced it. Parts 1–7 and the checklist are still typed/coded as normal.
:::

# Part 1 · Set up the document (→ see Lecture 05)

Create a new `.qmd` file and write YAML front matter that makes a **professional Word document** — a title, a table of contents, and numbered sections.

``` yaml
---
title: "..."
author: "Your Name"
date: today
format:
  docx:
    toc: true
    number-sections: true
    fig-width: 6
    fig-height: 4
---
```

# Part 2 · Bring in the analysis with named chunks (→ see Lecture 05, Worksheet 05)

Move your analysis into the report as **code chunks**. Follow the same habits as your scripts:

- one **library** chunk at the top
- a separate **load-data** chunk
- small chunks, each with a **unique label**

> **Q3 — How many code chunks does your report have?** \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
>
> **Q4 — List the label you gave your data-loading chunk:** \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

::: callout-warning
**⚠️ Watch out!** Quarto renders top to bottom in a **fresh session**. Load your libraries and data in chunks **above** anything that uses them, or the render will fail and name the broken chunk.
:::

# Part 7 · Push it further — cross-referencing (new material)

Everything so far was covered in Lecture 05/Worksheet 05. Quarto can also **number and cross-reference** your table and figure automatically, so your prose says "as shown in Table 1" and the number is never wrong even if you reorder things later.

Give your table chunk the label `#| label: tbl-summary` and a caption `#| tbl-cap: "..."`. Give your figure chunk `#| label: fig-leaf` and `#| fig-cap: "..."`. Then, in your Results prose, reference them by typing `@tbl-summary` and `@fig-leaf` instead of writing "the table above" or "the figure below."

Also add **one callout block** of your own — `::: callout-note`, `::: callout-warning`, or `::: callout-tip` — flagging one real caveat or limitation of your analysis (small sample size, an outlier you kept, an assumption you're not fully sure holds). You've seen dozens of these in the lecture slides; now write one about your own data.

# Part 8 · Predict, then check — by hand

**Before** you touch the YAML or any chunk options for this part, get a piece of paper.

By hand, sketch or describe: if you added `#| echo: false` to *only* the chunk that computes your group means/model (not the whole document), what exactly would change in the rendered Word document — and what would stay exactly the same? Be specific about which chunks are affected.

Then make that change, render, and — still by hand, under your prediction — write whether you were right, and if not, what actually happened.

# Part 9 · Explain it, by hand

Answer the following by hand, in your own words, as if explaining to a classmate who missed this unit — no textbook phrasing.

1.  Point to **one specific chunk in your own report** and explain why you set `echo` the way you did for *that* chunk specifically (not in general — for that one).

# Submission checklist

Before uploading to Canvas, confirm:

- [ ] Your `.qmd` file renders to Word with **no errors**
- [ ] The Word document has a **title, table of contents, and numbered sections**
- [ ] Libraries and data load in **named chunks** above everything that uses them
- [ ] At least **two numbers** in your prose come from **inline code**
- [ ] The report includes **one table** and **one figure**, both from code
- [ ] Your table and figure are **cross-referenced** by number in your prose (Part 7)
- [ ] Your report includes **one callout block** about a real limitation of your own analysis (Part 7)
- [ ] Introduction, Results, and Discussion sections are written
- [ ] Parts 8 and 9 are answered **by hand** and embedded as photos, not typed
- [ ] You are submitting **both** the `.qmd` and the rendered `.docx`
